findings.current: “Hold on, hyung. Let’s talk after you let go. Let go.”
findings.defect: Taekyung already calls Jin Wikyung “hyung,” so Wikyung’s immediate complaint that he said “hyungnim” and should use “hyung” has no logical trigger.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the intended contrast between the stiff “hyungnim” and the familiar “hyung,” preserving Wikyung’s complaint and the brothers’ established comic dynamic.
findings.replacement: “Hold on, hyungnim. Let’s talk after you let go. Let go.”

findings.current: “To be precise, when I first left Henan, my purpose was to find the murderers who killed the late Poison King Tang Sadok and the Heaven-Shaking Divine Nun. But the situation changed considerably along the way.”
findings.defect: Calling Tang Sadok “the late Poison King” directly contradicts the surrounding chapter, which establishes that he is unconscious and ends with his awakening.
findings.rationale: This preserves Jin Wikyung’s original understanding when he departed Henan while making clear that Tang Sadok’s reported death was mistaken, consistent with both the earlier coma reference and the chapter-ending awakening.
findings.replacement: “To be precise, when I first left Henan, my purpose was to find the murderers believed to have killed Poison King Tang Sadok and the Heaven-Shaking Divine Nun. But the situation changed considerably along the way.”
findings.source: Chapter 374, Tang Horyong and Jin Wikyung’s meeting
